messages:
sam_support: Hey team — Customer (acct: acme-corp) reporting embeddings failing after they 'upgraded' the model in our console. They used to get 1536-dim vectors, now requests error out with a dimension mismatch. stack trace attached in their support ticket.
sam_support: Quick summary from ticket: 
- Endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings
- Model they selected: rwd-embed-1536 -> they changed to rwd-embed-ml-v2 (auto-upgrade from UI)
- Error seen: 
  ValueError: Embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1600
- Affects their vector DB ingestion step (we think Pinecone)
- They pinned to the old model in UI and that fixed it temporarily but they need guidance on how to safely migrate.
customer_acct: @sam_support adding more context — we do batch inserts of 50 vectors, and the ingestion job fails halfway. We've rolled back to pinned model but want to migrate asap. Any ETA?
sam_support: Thanks — can you share the exact curl or SDK call you're using? Also, are you specifying a model_version param anywhere?
customer_acct: Here's our minimal curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ****" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-ml-v2","input":["doc1","doc2",...],"batch_size":50}'
```
customer_acct: We did not pass model_version — used the model alias from the console.
devin_engineering: Copying in devops. I suspect the new model alias maps to a different dimensionality (1600). The server should ideally return a clear header or error with expected dims.
maya_sre: tagging infra-bot: any infra logs for that time?
infra-bot: deploy noticed model alias rwd-embed-ml-v2 was updated at 2026-03-02T17:03:12Z -> underlying model id rwd-embed-1600-beta. No autoscaling events around failures.
devin_engineering: Repro attempt (local):
- Using our SDK with the customer's inputs in single and batch modes.
- Single input: returns vector length 1600 with model rwd-embed-ml-v2
- Batch of 2: same, but their ingestion pipeline expects 1536 and throws on DB side.
- Error we can produce with their client code:
```python
# pseudo reproduce
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key='REDACTED')
resp = c.embeddings.create(model='rwd-embed-ml-v2', input=['a','b'])
vec = resp['data'][0]['embedding']
len(vec) # -> 1600
# their code then runs: assert len(vec) == 1536 -> raises
```
devin_engineering: Root cause: alias pointed to new model with different vector size. The pinned model they created pointed to old model id and worked.
sam_support: Customer asks: why did the alias change without notice? They said they didn't update the model — UI suggested an "upgrade" with a button and they clicked.
devin_engineering: There are two flows: 1) alias auto-upgrades when there's a recommended patch (we email), 2) UI shows "upgrade available" that users must opt into. We need to confirm which one was used.
customer_acct: We definitely clicked the upgrade CTA in console. Might have missed the dims note. Tough UX.
maya_sre: Action items so far: 
- Confirm alias mapping history for their org (who changed it, when).
- Add guardrail to UI: surface embedding dims on upgrade banners.
- In the API layer, include X-Embedding-Dim header in responses.
- Short term: provide customer a script to detect dims and reformat or reject before DB ingestion.
devin_engineering: For immediate support to customer, propose a small client-side shim we can provide that will 1) call the embeddings endpoint for the first sample to detect dim, 2) validate all subsequent vectors, and 3) fail fast with actionable msg. Example script: 
```bash
# quick detect + validate
python - <<PY
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
first = client.embeddings.create(model='rwd-embed-ml-v2', input=['test'])
d = len(first['data'][0]['embedding'])
print('dim', d)
# raise if not expected
PY
```
This is low friction.
sam_support: Please paste the exact error message we'll send to the customer for their ingestion job. Need it to be non-technical.
devin_engineering: Suggestion for customer message: 
- "Your selected embedding model now returns 1600-dimensional vectors, but your ingestion pipeline expects 1536. To migrate, either pin your model to the old variant (temporary) or update your DB schema/ingestion to accept 1600-d vectors. We can provide a compatibility script to check vector size before ingesting."
customer_acct: If we update schema we might need to reindex. Is there a recommended migration path?
devin_engineering: Two options: 
1) Reindex: generate new embeddings for all docs with the new model (costly).
2) Use a projection shim: if dims differ by a small fixed amount, you can pad or truncate (only if semantic implications are acceptable — usually not recommended).
We should be explicit: truncation/padding is risky. Recommended: re-embed or keep old embeddings pinned until you can do a controlled reindex.
maya_sre: I'll pull audit logs and confirm who hit the UI upgrade CTA. Also adding a quick check to the console so upgrade prompts include a dim callout.
sam_support: Customer asked us to automate the detection on their org level and fail upgrades that would change dims without explicit confirmation. Can we do that?
devin_engineering: We can add an enforcement flag per org for breaking-change upgrades. Short timeline: small change in console + warning banner (2-3d). API change to include dim header (1d). Longer: enforceable org-level policy (2 weeks).
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: console-ui patch 'embed-dim-warning' -> staging 2026-03-18 04:00UTC.
sam_support: I'll reply to customer with steps: 
1) Pin back to previous model id if you need immediate stability (we can help).
2) Run the provided detect script to confirm dims for target model.
3) Plan reindex if moving forwards, or ask us for migration assistance.
Assigning to @devin_engineering to prepare the customer-facing script and to draft the internal PR for X-Embedding-Dim header.
devin_engineering: Acknowledged. I'll drop the script in their ticket and open a short-lived patch to add header & better error text for mismatch runtime error.
sam_support: Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket with the proposed messaging and the temporary script.
customer_acct: Appreciate the fast turnaround. We'll hold on the upgrade until we get the migration plan. :thumbsup:
